Foundry Art Batch 1

Wings of Freedom for Foundry VTT: Codex art batch 1 in the locked style (ADR-0022, ADR-0027). For owner review; nothing here is approved yet.

§1Action Catalog icons For review

42 icons, one per Action Catalog entry not approved in the style lock. ACTION pentagon frame, readability v2: two or three big shapes, thick strokes, no interior detail. Wax-seal red marks the arrowhead or the one accent. Plain ink on transparent, so on the dark ground they fade by design, like the approved set. Shown at 64, 32, and 24 px.

§2Token status icons For review

11 new status badges; with the approved Down and Grabbed the token set is 13. Filled ink disc, parchment keyline, status red #D6402F as the main state colour. Every state below is tracked in data/. The last swatch pins the 24 px badge to a token.

Dropped candidates

  • Blind Spot: A Position, not a status: it is held relative to each Focus Titan separately (data/gear/sheet-fields.yaml, positions), and the website's pos-blind-spot icon already covers it.
  • Apart: The default relation to every Foe (data/skirmish/skirmish.yaml: every soldier starts Apart), tracked per soldier-Foe pair; a token badge would be on almost always. Engaged carries the information.

§6Notes and prompts

  • Counts: 42 action icons, 11 status icons, 2 foe plates, 8 Soldier portraits, 1 setup plate: 64 assets, 90 Codex jobs (64 first tries and 26 retries across 19 assets, at most 3 tries each).
  • Status list from data/: Pinned (harm sheet field pinned), Airborne (gear sheet field airborne), Jammed (derived jammed, squad sheet mark J), Overloaded (derived overloaded, mark O), Lame horse (derived lame, mark L), Mounted (horse.mounted, mark M), Engaged (skirmish.yaml engaged_apart), Carrying and Carried (sheet fields carrying and carried_by), Untreated Critical Injury (critical_injuries treated false), and Held (skirmish.yaml held, a person's Grapple; added from data, not on the candidate list).
  • Dropped: Blind Spot (a Position held per Focus Titan; the website's pos-blind-spot icon covers it) and Apart (the default per-Foe relation; Engaged carries the information).
  • Every icon was proofed at 32 and 24 px (downscaled, then enlarged with nearest neighbour to check for blur) on paper and on a dark ground. Retries are listed under each item.
  • Status red #D6402F is used on status badges only; action icons keep the wax-seal red accent, as in the approved set.
  • Weakest items: Mount or Dismount (the stirrup still reads a little like a flask), Reload (the musket is thin at 32 px; the powder-horn idea was ignored by the model), Sneak (busy at 24 px), Body Part strike (thin blade), Leap Clear and Performance roll (readable but not instant).
  • md5 duplicate check over originals/ and rejected/: no duplicates.
  • Web copies in foundry/art-src/batch-1/web/: icons 256 px webp with alpha, portraits and foes 512 px long edge, setup 1920 px wide; cwebp -q 82 -alpha_q 100 -m 6.
  • Prompts are in foundry/art-src/batch-1/prompts/ (retries as -a2, -a3). They reuse the style-lock v2 blocks word for word; only the reference line and the frame's 'keep exactly as in' wording change. Two samples are below.
Action icon, Read action-read.txt
Use the `board-game-icon-assets` skill for this task (read its SKILL.md and references/icon-principles.md first and follow them). Use your built-in image generation tool to create exactly ONE stamp icon for a tabletop RPG website, then copy the generated PNG into the current working directory under the exact filename listed below (copy the file; do not re-encode, crop, or resize it). Do not create or modify any other files, do not write code, and do not review anything; only generate and copy the image. When done, reply with only the absolute path of the saved file and one line naming its glyph.

COPY GUARD: copy only the exact file paths your own image generation calls returned in this session. Never copy the newest file in ~/.codex/generated_images, which other sessions running in parallel also write to.

Aspect ratio 1:1 (1024x1024).

REFERENCE IMAGES: the attached colour plates are world reference only (what Survey Corps soldiers, ODM gear, and blades look like), not how to render; never copy their detail. The attached flat stamp icons (the hexagon feather, the ring with a turning arrow, and the teardrop with a lying figure) show the level of simplicity wanted: big flat shapes, thick strokes, almost no detail. The attached pentagon icons are APPROVED members of this same family: copy their frame exactly (shape, size, position, stroke weight, ink colour, stamp texture) and their level of simplicity, and draw only the new glyph below inside it. Do not copy their glyphs.

ICON SYSTEM (locked for every icon):
- Stamp icons printed like a rubber stamp or a woodcut: ink on paper. One ink, iron-gall brown-black #29241D, plus one red accent (see the frame block for which red), used sparingly and never as the only cue.
- Bold, chunky, flat shapes; one thick consistent stroke of about 7 percent of canvas width; slightly rough stamp edges with a light ink speckle inside the solid areas. No gradients, no shading, no 3D, no glow, no drop shadows, no perspective: flat front-on view.
- Square 1024x1024 canvas. The icon is centred and its frame's outer edge sits exactly within the central 84 percent of the canvas (8 percent empty margin on each side).
- Background: transparent with true alpha. If transparency is not available, a plain flat pure white #FFFFFF background with nothing else on it (no paper texture, no shadow, no vignette).
- No text, letters, numerals, or logos anywhere.
- No electronics shapes and no modern machine parts. The world is pre-industrial.

READABILITY (v2, owner-locked; players see these icons at 32 and 64 px, and status icons at 24 to 32 px on map tokens):
- Every icon must read clearly at 32 px. Design it as a 32 px pictogram first, then draw it large.
- One bold silhouette per icon, built from two or three big shapes at most (count the frame as zero). If a shape would not survive at 32 px, leave it out.
- Thick strokes only: nothing thinner than the frame stroke, about 7 percent of canvas width. No hairlines, no thin limbs, no fingers drawn one by one, no small props, no tiny gaps or counters.
- Figures are blocky pictograms: a solid round head (no face, no hair) and one simple solid body block (a hooded cloak wedge or a rounded bar). No arms or legs unless the pose needs one, and then as one thick stub.
- No interior detail: no texture, folds, muscles, knuckles, wrinkles, straps, rivets, or shading lines inside a shape. The only texture allowed is a light stamp speckle and a slightly rough stamp edge.
- Leave generous empty space between the glyph shapes and the frame.
- Status red: on STATUS icons the main state colour is a bright signal red #D6402F (contrast about 3.6:1 against the ink disc #241F1B and about 3.3:1 against the parchment keyline #E4DCC5). Never use the dark wax-seal red #8B2A21 on the ink disc; it disappears at 24 px.

FRAME (keep exactly as in the attached approved pentagon icons):
- ACTION frame: a thick ink upright pentagon, point at the top centre, flat bottom edge, straight sides, slightly softened corners, same stroke as the reference, transparent inside. The glyph sits in the lower, wider part of the pentagon and fills about 70 percent of its inner area. Accent colour for action icons: wax-seal red #8B2A21, on arrowheads and marks only.

ICON:
FILENAME: action-read.png
Meaning: Read: Instinct. Study a Titan to learn its Next Behavior and other facts.
Glyph, exactly two shapes:
1. In the centre, ONE Titan head seen in side profile facing left, as ONE plain solid ink shape: an oversized round skull, a slack open jaw shown only as a notch in the outline, and a short thick neck. No face details, no hair, no lines inside.
2. Around it, FOUR thick wax-seal red corner brackets (L shapes), one at each corner of an imaginary square framing the head, like a sighting frame. Each bracket arm is as thick as the frame stroke. The brackets never touch the head or the pentagon.
Direction cue: focus, inward.
EXCLUSIONS: no text, no letters, no numerals, no logos, no plus signs, no crosses, no stars, no faces, no hair, no belts or straps, no swords, no crossguards, no shields, no hearts, no speed lines, no background colour, no paper texture behind the icon.
Default Soldier portrait, Medic (retry) portrait-medic-a2.txt
REFERENCE IMAGES: the attached images are approved plates from this same set. Match their rendering exactly: the same anime linework, painterly anime shading, muted warm palette, and level of stylisation. Do not copy their subjects.

Use your built-in image generation tool to create exactly ONE image, then copy the generated PNG into the current working directory, using only the exact file path your own image generation call returned in this session (never the newest file in ~/.codex/generated_images, which other sessions also write to), under the filename given below (copy the file; do not re-encode, crop, or resize it). Do not create or modify any other files, do not write code, and do not review anything. When done, reply with only the absolute path of the saved file.

FILENAME: portrait-medic-v2.png
Aspect ratio 4:5 (for example 1024x1280).

STYLE (locked, colour plate): Semi-realistic anime illustration, the high-end cinematic version of a premium dark-fantasy military anime, like a still from a theatrical anime film. Characters drawn with clean, confident dark linework and soft painterly anime shading; grounded human anatomy and proportions; accurate costume, leather, and metal equipment detail; detailed hand-painted backgrounds with visible brush texture. Not chibi, not photorealistic, not a 3D render, not Western comic style, not glossy digital concept art. Colour: slightly muted, warm, filmic palette that sits well mounted on aged paper, like a faded colour plate bound into an old field manual. Parchment and dust tones (#E4DCC5), iron-gall ink brown-black shadows (#29241D), deep military green (#2F4B3C), gunmetal steel (#56605F), muted flesh and earth (#B38467), dark cloth green (#16211B), with only a sparing wax-seal red accent (#8B2A21). Lifted blacks, restrained saturation, soft film grain, gentle vignette.

WORLD: a walled, 19th-century-inspired world behind colossal stone Walls fifty metres tall. Survey Corps soldiers wear a short tan cropped field jacket, white shirt, white fitted trousers, dark brown leather harness straps crossing the chest, hips, and thighs, knee-high brown boots, and a hooded dark green cloak with the Wings of Freedom emblem (two overlapping stylised wings, one white and one blue, on a small shield) on the back. Omni-directional mobility (ODM) gear sits at the hips: a steel gas canister and a long rectangular blade scabbard box on each hip, and a compact grappling-hook launcher unit at the lower back.

SUBJECT: a portrait plate of a Survey Corps Medic, a default soldier portrait for the Medic Specialty.
Head first: a gentle-faced young man in his mid-twenties of South Asian descent with warm brown skin, thick wavy chestnut-brown hair cut short, a short neat beard, dark brown eyes, and a small mole on his left cheekbone; a kind, concentrated expression. He wears the full Survey Corps uniform and ODM gear from the world block, hood down unless stated, cloak hanging behind. Any ODM blade shown is a long, perfectly straight, uniform-width steel strip with an oblique squared tip, divided into snap-off segments by diagonal score gaps like a box-cutter blade, fixed to a chunky pistol-like trigger handle with a trigger guard, with no crossguard and no pommel.
His jacket sleeves are rolled up. He is winding a white linen bandage from a roll in his hands, a leather medical satchel on his hip, and a plain white cloth band around his upper arm (no symbol on it).
Scene: half-length portrait from the waist up, three-quarter view, turned slightly left, inside a canvas field hospital tent, cots and hanging lanterns softly out of focus behind him.
Light and mood: warm lantern light mixed with cool daylight from the tent flap; tired but steady care.
The face is original and specific, clearly not any canon character.

RETRY NOTE: the first attempt painted a red cross on the medical satchel. There must be NO cross or medical symbol anywhere: the satchel is plain brown leather with a buckled flap, and the armband is plain white cloth.

EXCLUSIONS: no text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, no signage, no watermarks, no signatures, no borders or frames, no logos except the wing emblem where the uniform carries it. Original characters only: no recognisable canon characters (not Levi, Eren, Mikasa, Armin, Erwin, Hange, or any other named character likeness) and no named canon Titans. No extra or missing fingers or limbs, no malformed horses, no modern objects, no firearms. No soldier with a black bob, messy black hair, long dark hair, a ponytail, or a man bun.
